sections.overview: Nomada basalis is a cuckoo bee recorded across Europe and nearby regions; its known hosts are Andrena mining bees.
sections.identification: A French account gives females as 10–12 mm and males as 8–11 mm; use a key for identification.
sections.habitat: It is recorded across the Palearctic, but no characteristic habitat is established.
sections.diet: Like other Nomada, the female does not provision her own brood with pollen; the larva develops in a host nest and consumes its food stores.
sections.behavior: Reported hosts are Andrena truncatilabris and A. optata; further hosts are possible.
sections.reproduction: It is cleptoparasitic; species-specific flight and brood details remain uncertain.
sections.ecology: The European Red List classifies N. basalis as Least Concern; this continental assessment does not establish abundance at any particular locality.
sections.conservation: No species-specific conservation measure was established here; protecting host nesting habitat is a cautious general implication, not a documented targeted programme.
